source.title: Hippocampal replay is not a simple function of experience
authors: Matthijs A A van der Meer

confidence_rationale: Directed at MECH-023's third CONFIRMING criterion -- that hypothesis-tagged (simulated / replayed) content must NOT shape the geometry the way real commitment does. Gupta et al. show hippocampal replay covers physically available but never-traversed trajectories and over-represents the LESS-practised routes, so the map is demonstrably rehearsing paths the animal did not take. If replay writes back into the same map that carries harm history, the clean real-versus-simulated separation REE enforces at accumulate() has no straightforward biological warrant. Held at 0.62 because the paper shows replay CONTENT, not that replay deforms the residue-bearing geometry -- the inference to a write-back is mine, not theirs.
failure_signatures: Replay content is not proportional to experience: sequence B was replayed frequently after more than ten minutes of performing sequence A, and less-frequently-run routes were replayed MORE than heavily practised ones. A REE residue field updated by anything replay-like would accumulate along paths never actually committed to.
Replay covered never-experienced novel shortcut trajectories -- the strongest form of the problem, since there is no real committed episode anywhere in the animal's history for that path.

The paper does not measure whether these replayed sequences produce plasticity in the same substrate that stores aversive history, so the challenge it poses to the MECH-094 gate is structural rather than demonstrated. Treat it as a design warning, not as disconfirming evidence.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In rats performing two distinct behavioural sequences, hippocampal replay during sharp-wave ripples did not simply mirror recent experience: sequence B was replayed frequently even after more than ten minutes of performing sequence A, replay covered all physically available trajectories including never-experienced novel paths, and less-frequently-performed routes were replayed more often than heavily practised ones.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-023's third CONFIRMING criterion imports the MECH-094 gate: hypothesis-tagged harm in region R must NOT produce the rank divergence that real harm produces, because only what was actually done is supposed to shape the geometry. REE enforces this by construction -- ResidueField.accumulate refuses hypothesis-tagged content. This paper is the reason that enforcement should be treated as an architectural DECISION with a cost, not as a biological fact being modelled: the biological system that ARC-013 names as the residue substrate spends its offline time traversing paths the animal never took, weighted inversely to how much it actually did take them.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The inferential step from 'replay includes never-experienced trajectories' to 'simulated content deforms the harm-history geometry' is not made by the authors and is not measured here. Replay could be entirely read-only with respect to the residue-bearing map, in which case there is no tension at all. What the paper establishes is that the simulation channel is rich, promiscuous and not experience-proportional -- which makes the write-back question live rather than answering it.
mapping.source_context: Rat hippocampal ensemble recording during sharp-wave ripple events on a multi-route maze task with two distinct behavioural sequences.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality -- a heavily cited Neuron paper whose central finding has held up. Mapping fidelity is the limiting term: the paper is about replay content and REE's question is about write permissions, one inferential step away.
